questions.question: What is the other name for the unit Coulomb/second?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **Ampere (A).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Coulomb Per Second (C/s)** is a unit in the category of **Electric current.**
 
• It is also known as coulombs per second, (coulomb/second).
 
• This unit is commonly used in the **SI unit **system.
 
• Coulomb Per Second (C/s) has a dimension of I where **I is electric current.**
 
• **1 coulomb** of charge flows through any cross-section of a conductor in 1 second, the electric current through it is said to be 1 ampere.
 
• The **SI unit **of current is coulomb per second, generally known as **ampere.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Second-**

 
• The **second **(s or sec) is the International System of Units **(SI) unit of time** measurement.
 
• It is the time required for an electromagnetic (EM) field to propagate **299,792,458 meters (2.99792458 x 10⁸ m)** through a vacuum.
 
• This figure is sometimes rounded to 3 x 10⁸ m, or 300,000 kilometers (3 x 10⁵ km).
 
• **One second **is equal to **1/86,400** of a mean solar day.
 
• This is easy to derive from the fact that there are 60 seconds in a minute, 60 minutes in an hour and 24 hours in a mean solar day.

**Joule-**

 
• It is equal to the **amount of work done** when a force of** one newton displaces a mass through a distance of one metre **in the direction of that force.
 
• It is also the energy dissipated as heat when an electric current of one ampere passes through a resistance of one ohm for one second.

**Volt-**

 
• **Unit of electrical potential**, potential difference and electromotive force in the metre–kilogram–second system (SI).
 
• It is equal to the** difference in potential between two points in a conductor carrying one-ampere current **when the power dissipated between the points is one watt.

questions.question: Which of the following theory said that bond is formed between two atoms either by sharing or transfer of valence electrons?
questions.solution:
**Explanation:**

**Valency:**

The valence or valency of an element in chemistry is a measurement of how well it can combine with other atoms to form chemical compounds or molecules.

**Types of Bonds:**

Chemical bonds, also known as electrical forces, can be categorized into five different groups: ionic, covalent, metallic, van der Waals, and hydrogen bonds.

**Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion Theory:**

 
• Based on the number of valence shell electron bond pairs between the atoms in a molecule or ion, the valence shell electron pair repulsion (VSEPR) theory is a model used to predict 3-D molecular shape.
 
• According to this hypothesis, electron pairs will position themselves to reduce the consequences of their mutual repulsion.
 
• In a molecule, electrons remain as far away from one another. Covalent bonds also contain electrons in addition to lone pairs.
 
• To reduce repulsion and increase molecular stability, electron pairs will repel away from one another.

**Valance Bond Theory:**

 
• The electrical structure of molecules is described by the valence bond theory.
 
• According to the hypothesis, electrons fill each of an atom's atomic orbitals inside a molecule, and the nucleus of one atom is drawn to the electrons of another atom.

**Molecular Orbital Theory:**

 
• According to the molecular orbital hypothesis, every atom has a tendency to group together to create molecular orbitals.
 
• As a result of this configuration, electrons can be found in a variety of atomic orbitals and are frequently linked to diverse nuclei.

**Electronic Theory of Chemical Bonding:**

 
• The electronic theory of valence was created by Kossel and Lewis to explain how chemical bonds are formed between two atoms.
 
• By losing, acquiring, or sharing electrons, every atom strives to achieve octet configuration (the presence of eight electrons in its valence shell).

questions.question:
Identify the statements that are false:

(A) Charge becomes used up as it flows through a circuit.

(B) Charge flows through circuits at very high speeds.

(C) A light bulb transforms the electrical energy of moving charge into other forms of energy.

(D) The charge carriers in wires are simply the electrons possessed by the atoms that make up the wires.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(A) and (B).**__

__**Explanation:**__

**(A) Charge becomes used up as it flows through a circuit.** **(FALSE)**

__
 
• Charge is** conserved in a closed circuit__**.
 
• It doesn't get used up; instead, **it flows continuously from one point to another.**

**(B) Charge flows through circuits at very high speeds. (FALSE)**

__
 
• In most circuits, the charge carriers (usually electrons) **move relatively slowly.**__
 
• Although the electrical signals (changes in voltage and current) can travel at close to the speed of light in conductors, the actual movement of electrons is much slower. 

**(C) A light bulb transforms the electrical energy of moving charge into other forms of energy. (TRUE)**

__
 
• When an electric current passes through a light bulb, the filament heats up and emits light, **converting the electrical energy into light energy and some heat energy.**__

**(D) The charge carriers in wires are simply the electrons possessed by the atoms that make up the wires**.** (TRUE)**

__
 
• In most electrical wires, **the charge carriers are electrons, which are the negatively charged particles orbiting the atoms in the wire.**__
 
• These electrons move through the wire, creating an electric current when a voltage is applied.

questions.question: Cope's Rule, often discussed in the context of evolutionary biology, is best described by which of the following statements?

options.text: It states that animals within a population tend to evolve to smaller sizes over time.
It states that, over evolutionary time, the body sizes of certain groups of animals may increase.
It emphasizes the tendency of species to maintain a constant body size throughout their evolutionary history.
It suggests that species will exhibit an increase in complexity as they evolve.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 2.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• Indian Express: Why big animals got smaller, even before climate change

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__****Cope's Rule:**

 
• Cope's Rule is a **hypothesis in evolutionary biology.**
 
• It suggests a **directional trend in the evolution of body sizes within certain groups of animals.**
 
• The hypothesis is **named after the American paleontologist Edward Drinker Cope.**
 
• According to Cope's Rule, over evolutionary time, the body sizes of species within a particular lineage or group may tend to increase.
 
• The **general trend implies that the descendants of a particular group of organisms may be larger than their ancestors. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Cope's Rule has been **observed in various vertebrate and invertebrate groups.**
 
• The **increase in body size is thought to confer advantages such as enhanced competitiveness, better predatory capabilities, or improved survival in changing environments.**
 
• While Cope's Rule **suggests a general trend, it is not a universal rule, and exceptions exist in the evolutionary record.**
 
• The hypothesis contributes to our** understanding of long-term patterns in the evolution of organismal size.**

questions.question: The polio virus affects the child's system most-
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The nervous system.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Poliovirus, which causes **polio, primarily affects the nervous system,** particularly the **motor neurons in the spinal cord.**
 
• This can lead to** muscle weakness and paralysis,** typically in the legs, which are the** hallmark symptoms of this disease.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Polio, or poliomyelitis, is a **severe infectious disease** caused by the** poliovirus.**
 
• This disease can** damage the nervous system **and cause **paralysis.**
 
• The poliovirus is **primarily transmitted via the fecal-oral route.**
 
• That means it **typically starts in the digestive system**, where the virus can** multiply.**
 
• However, it's the **nervous system that the polio virus** affects most.
 
• Once the poliovirus enters the body,** it multiplies in the throat and intestines.**
 
• In some cases,** it can enter the bloodstream and reach the central nervous system** (the brain and spinal cord), where it targets the **motor neurons.**
 
• **Motor neurons are nerve cells that send signals** from the **brain and spinal cord to your muscles**, controlling their movement.
 
• Once the poliovirus **damages these motor neurons**, it can cause** muscle weakness and paralysis**.
 
• This is because when **motor neurons are destroyed,** the muscles they contro**l can't receive signals from the brain**, causing them to** become weak and flaccid.**
 
• In severe cases, if the **muscles used for breathing become paralyzed**, the disease can be **fatal.**

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding INSACOG (India SARS-CoV-2 Genome Consortium).

1. INSACOG will prioritise developing and expanding a SARS-CoV-2 sewage surveillance program.

2. The CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology, which is also part of the INSACOG network, has since early 2020 been collecting sewage from large drains in cities to check for the presence of the virus.

3. Delta (B.1.617.2 and AY.x) continues to be the main VOC (Variant of Concern) in India. No new VOI (Variant of Interest) or VOC are noted in India.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1, 2 and 3.**__

__**In News**__

__
 
• **The decline in daily new infections across India has prompted INSACOG (India SARS-CoV-2 Genome Consortium), the consortium of labs focused on sequencing coronavirus variants, to “prioritise” new surveillance approaches.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• In view of currently declining cases and the importance of early detection of increased transmission in the future, INSACOG will prioritise developing and expanding a SARS-CoV-2 sewage surveillance program. **Hence statement 1 is correct.**
 
• The CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology, which is also part of the INSACOG network, has since early 2020 been collecting sewage from large drains in cities to check for the presence of the virus. Hence statement 2 is correct.
 
• Because a large fraction of those afflicted by the virus are asymptomatic but are carriers of infection, their body fluids and stool often contain traces of the virus.
 
• Finding large proportions of it in public drains can often be a precursor to a fresh outbreak, with a rise in symptomatic infections.
 
• Delta (B.1.617.2 and AY.x) continues to be the main VOC (Variant of Concern) in India. No new VOI (Variant of Interest) or VOC are noted in India. Hence statement 3 is correct.

questions.question: When a piece of stone tied to a thread is rotated on a horizontal circular path, then velocity of the piece of stone at a point will act along :

options.text: perpendicular to the circular path acting outward along radius of the circle
tangential to the circular path at that point
perpendicular to the plane of the circular path.
toward centre of the circular path

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**tangential to the circular path at that point**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **When an object is moving in a circular path, its velocity at any given point is tangential to the circular path at that point.**
 
• This is because **velocity is a vector quantity,** meaning it has both magnitude (speed) and direction.
 
• The **direction of the velocity is always along the path of the object's motion.**
 
• In the case of circular motion, the path curves away from the straight line tangent to the circle, so the object is always "trying" to move off in the tangential direction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** direction of the centrifugal force **(an apparent force that acts outward on a body moving in a circular path) is **perpendicular to the circular path acting outward along the radius of the circle**.
 
• The **direction of the centripetal force** (the force causing the object to follow a curved path),** towards the center of the circular path.**

questions.question: Which of the following is the Method related to the teaching of science subjects?

options.text: Teacher centered and student oriented method

questions.solution:
“Science does not simply sit down & pray for things to happen but seeks to find out why things happen. It experiments and tries again and again and sometimes fails and sometimes succeeds & so bit by bit it adds to human knowledge. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

All the methods of teaching science can be classified into two types:-

**(i) Teacher-Centred and 

(ii) Pupil-Centred

(i) Teacher-Centred Methods:-**This type of teaching method focuses on telling, memorizing, recalling information. The student's participation is very limited wherein they only ask questions or answers questions. Most of the time the students are passive listeners and receive the knowledge. The teacher is the center of the process that goes on in the classroom. **Eg. Lecture method, Explanation method, Demonstration method, etc. 

(ii) Pupil-Centred Methods:- **This process emphasizes on need, requirement, interest, and capability of students. The students are active participants wherein their skills and abilities are developed. The climate in the classroom is conducive where flexibility is there. Teacher and students jointly explore the different aspects of the problem. **Eg. Laboratory method, Observation method, Search and find(Heuristic method), project method, test method, etc. **

__
 
• **Search and find method(Heuristic method)- **Through this method, students are made active independent enquirers and they are indulging in various activities through which important scientific information can be gathered. 

 
 
• Under this method, it is believed that every science lesson should be presented in the form of an inquiry in front of students.
 
• The main feature of scientific work is that it springs from a desire to know from our own knowledge some definite thing concerning which curiosity has come to an end.
 
 
 
• **Test method: **A test method is a method for a test in science or engineering, such as a physical test, chemical test, or statistical test. It is a definitive procedure that produces a test result. 
 
 
• A test can be considered an observation or experiment that determines one or more characteristics of a given sample, product, process, or service.
 
 
 
• ​**Explanation** method: The most basic teaching method is an explanation. The explanation is characterized by its function as "a tool that is used by a speaker for understanding or 'giving a sense to the object of communication, of a debate, or a discussion.
 
 
• The role of an explanation is to make clearer the meaning of an object (method, term, assignment) maintaining formally the necessary distance between the object of the action or study and the tools. In the learning/teaching process, the explanation is a tool used by both, teachers and students.
 
• Its goal is to manifest comprehension.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points __In this context, the teaching of science gain significant importance and it needs an appropriate method. So it is important to know about the different methods of teaching science and to be able to choose the appropriate method in a classroom.

 
• The methods are namely lecture method, demonstration method, lecture cum demonstration method, laboratory method, **heuristic method (search and explore method)**, assignment method, project method, a problem-solving method, question and answer method, **explanation method, test method**, role-playing method, brainstorming method, and innovative method.
 
• It is up to a teacher's discretion to choose the method which is most suitable for a certain topic in a certain class and sometimes a teacher should introduce different methods in a lesson plan to address the learning styles of the students.

Hence, we can conclude that the right answer to this question is All of the above.

questions.question: Hot air balloon rises up because

options.text: hot air is lighter than cold air
hot air has a higher pressure
hot air has a lower pressure

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**hot air is lighter than cold air**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hot air balloon **rises up because **hot air is lighter than cold air**.
 
• Hot air is less dense than cold air. When the air inside the balloon is heated, it becomes less dense than the surrounding air, which causes it to rise.
 
• The balloon rises until it reaches a level where the density of the hot air inside the balloon is equal to the density of the surrounding air. At this point, the balloon reaches equilibrium and stops rising.
 
• The amount of lift generated by the hot air depends on the temperature difference between the air inside the balloon and the surrounding air. The greater the temperature difference, the greater the lift.
 
• Hot air balloons are designed to be able to control their altitude by adjusting the temperature of the air inside the balloon. By heating the air, the balloon can rise, and by cooling the air, it can descend.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Hot air has higher energy. This statement is not correct, as the energy content of air is not directly related to its ability to lift a balloon. While it is true that hot air has more thermal energy than cold air, this energy does not directly translate into lift.
 
• Hot air has a higher pressure. This statement is not correct, as hot air actually has a lower pressure than cold air. This is because the molecules in hot air are more spread out than in cold air, which leads to a lower density and lower pressure.
 
• Hot air has a lower pressure. This statement is correct, as explained above.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an active sensor used in remote sensing ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Radar**__.

__**Concept:**__

**Remote Sensing: **

It is the** art and science of obtaining information about an object without physical contact with that object.**

**Passive sensors:**

__
 
• Passive sensors **detect natural energy** (like sunlight) **that is reflected, emitted, or transmitted by objects in the environment.**
 
• Examples of passive sensors include optical cameras, infrared sensors, and multispectral/hyperspectral sensors that capture various wavelengths of light.

**Active sensors**

 
• Active sensors are **useful in situations where passive sensors might not work well,** such as in cloudy or rainy conditions, or when direct sunlight is not available.
 
• They can also **provide information about the structure and properties of objects that passive sensors might miss.**
 
• **The most common active sensor used in remote sensing is “radar”.**

**Explanation:**__

**Radar (Radio Detection and Ranging):**

__
 
• **Radar is an active remote sensing technology **that u**ses radio waves to detect and measure the properties of objects on the Earth's surface.**
 
• It emits radio waves and then measures the time it takes for the waves to bounce back after they have interacted with the target.
 
• **Radar can provide valuable information about the shape, size, and composition of objects, as well as their movement.**
 
• It is commonly used in applications such as weather monitoring, terrain mapping, and even satellite imagery of Earth.

Thus, **Radar is an example of an active sensor used in remote sensing.**__

questions.question: Which part of the human brain controls balance and coordination?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cerebellum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The cerebellum is located at the back of the brain, underneath the occipital lobes.
 
• It plays a crucial role in motor control, particularly in coordinating voluntary movements.
 
• The cerebellum helps maintain balance and posture by integrating sensory information from the spinal cord and other parts of the brain.
 
• It is involved in motor learning, allowing the body to perform smooth, accurate, and balanced movements.
 
• Damage to the cerebellum can result in ataxia, which is characterized by a lack of coordination and control over movements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cerebrum**

 
 
• The cerebrum is the largest part of the human brain and is responsible for higher brain functions such as thought, action, and sensory processing.
 
• It is divided into two hemispheres, each of which is further divided into lobes responsible for different functions.
 
• The cerebrum controls voluntary muscle movements and is involved in cognitive functions like learning and memory.
 
 
 
• **Medulla**
 
 
• The medulla oblongata is located in the brainstem and controls autonomic functions like breathing, heart rate, and blood pressure.
 
• It acts as a relay station, transmitting signals between the brain and the spinal cord.
 
 
 
• **Hypothalamus**
 
 
• The hypothalamus is a small region located below the thalamus and is crucial for maintaining homeostasis in the body.
 
• It regulates various autonomic functions such as temperature control, hunger, thirst, and circadian rhythms.
 
• The hypothalamus also plays a role in hormone secretion through its interaction with the pituitary gland.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an exothermic reaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Combustion of fuel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **combustion of fuel** is a chemical reaction between fuel and an oxidant, releasing energy in the form of heat and light.
 
• This process is **exothermic** because it releases more energy than it absorbs.
 
• Common examples of fuels include hydrocarbons such as **gasoline, diesel, and natural gas**.
 
• The energy released during combustion is utilized in various applications such as **power generation, heating, and propulsion**.
 
• Combustion reactions are crucial in industries and everyday life, driving engines and generating electricity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Exothermic Reactions**

 
 
• Exothermic reactions are chemical reactions that **release energy** in the form of heat.
 
• These reactions typically involve the breaking of bonds in reactants and the formation of new bonds in products, with a net release of energy.
 
• Examples include combustion, respiration, and many oxidation-reduction reactions.
 
• The released energy often increases the temperature of the surroundings.
 
 
 
• **Endothermic Reactions**
 
 
• Endothermic reactions are chemical reactions that **absorb energy** from their surroundings.
 
• These reactions require an input of energy to proceed, typically in the form of heat.
 
• Examples include photosynthesis, melting of ice, and evaporation of water.
 
• Endothermic reactions result in a decrease in the temperature of the surroundings.
 
 
 
• **Combustion Process**
 
 
• Combustion involves a rapid chemical reaction between a fuel and an oxidant, producing heat and light.
 
• It usually produces **carbon dioxide (CO2)** and **water (H2O)** as byproducts.
 
• Incomplete combustion can produce carbon monoxide (CO) and other harmful substances.
 
• Proper ventilation and control of fuel-to-oxidant ratio are crucial to ensure complete combustion.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Combustion**
 
 
• Combustion is widely used in **power plants** to generate electricity.
 
• It is the driving force behind **internal combustion engines** in vehicles.
 
• Combustion is essential in **heating systems** such as furnaces and boilers.
 
• It plays a key role in various industrial processes, including metal smelting and waste incineration.

questions.question: The power of fighting the diseases in the body is called:
questions.solution:
• The correct answer is __**Immunity power.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The body's **capability to resist or fight off diseases** and infections is called **immunity.**
 
• It is **facilitated by the immune system**, which is a network of cells, tissues and organs **working together to defend the body from harmful pathogens.**
 
• **Disinfection **usually refers to the **process of killing or removing harmful organisms **from surfaces or objects and is not a term generally used to describe the body's internal disease-fighting capability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Immunity system is a **complex network of cells, tissues, and organs that work together to defend the body against attacks by "foreign" **invaders such as bacteria, viruses, and other infectious** organisms that cause disease.**
 
• This process of defense is called "immunity." **There are two main components:** **innate immunity and adaptive immunity.**
 
• **Innate immunity:**

 
• This is our** first line of defense and is non-specific, **meaning it doesn't target specific threats.
 
• It includes** physical defense mechanisms like skin** (which blocks entry of pathogens) **and chemical defense mechanisms like enzymes in bodily fluids** (which break down pathogens).

 
• **Adaptive immunity:**

 
• This is an **antigen-specific immune response,** meaning it **targets specific pathogens.**
 
• If the body encounters a** threat that it has seen before**, the immune response can be **faster and stronger because the immune system "remembers" **the pathogen.
 
• This is why you typically **don't get diseases **like chickenpox more than once.

questions.question:
Match the scientist with their contribution:

 
 

 Scientist
 Contribution
 
 

 I. Lord Kelvin
 B. Heliocentric model
 
 

 II. Newton
 A. Laws of motion
 
 

 III. Einstein
 C. Theory of relativity
 
 

 IV. Copernicus 
 D. Laws of thermodynamics
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lord Kelvin **made foundational contributions to the **laws of thermodynamics **and the Kelvin scale of temperature.
 
• **Isaac Newton** formulated the** Laws of Motion**, which are fundamental principles of classical mechanics.
 
• **Albert Einstein** developed the** Theory of Relativity**, which includes the famous equation E=mc².
 
• **Nicholas Copernicus** introduced the **Heliocentric model**, which challenged the geocentric model of the universe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Heliocentric Model:** This astronomical model places the Sun at the center of the universe with planets, including Earth, revolving around it. It was revolutionary in changing our understanding of the cosmos.
 
• **Laws of Motion:** Newton's three laws describe the relationship between a body and the forces acting on it, and its motion in response to those forces.
 
• **Theory of Relativity:** Einstein's theory revolutionized physics with its concepts of space-time and the relationship between mass and energy.
 
• **Copernican Revolution:** The shift from the geocentric model (Earth-centered) to the heliocentric model marked a pivotal change in scientific thought, leading to the Scientific Revolution.
 
• **Laws of Thermodynamics:** The formulation of these laws was a gradual process, shaped by contributions from various scientists, including Lord Kelvin, Rudolf Clausius, James Clerk Maxwell, and others.

questions.question: Excessive consumption of ethanol causes damage to the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Liver.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ethanol, also known as alcohol, is metabolized primarily in the liver.**
 
• The liver is responsible for **detoxifying harmful substances in the body, including alcohol.**
 
• When alcohol is consumed in a moderate amount,** the liver can usually process it without substantial harm.**
 
• However, **excessive and prolonged intake of alcohol can overwhelm the liver's ability to metabolize alcohol, leading to the accumulation of toxic substances, inflammation, and damage.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Key impacts of excessive alcohol consumption on the liver:**

 
• **Alcoholic Hepatitis: **This is inflammation of the liver caused by excessive alcohol drinking over a prolonged period. Symptoms can include jaundice (yellowing of the skin and eyes), loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, fever, abdominal pain, and tenderness.
 
• **Cirrhosis:** This is the late stage of serious liver diseases. Continual damage to the liver causes scar tissue replacing healthy tissue, which blocks the flow of blood through the liver, preventing it from functioning properly.
 
• **Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease:** This is the earliest stage of alcohol-related liver disease and the most common alcohol-related disease. Fat builds up in the liver, making it harder for it to function.
 
• **Alcoholic Liver Disease (ALD): **This refers to a range of conditions and associated symptoms related to heavy alcohol use.

questions.question:
Identify the correct statement:

 Assertion (A): Ancient modes of transportation were less efficient compared to modern ones.

Reason (B): The invention of the wheel did not significantly impact transportation methods.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 2) Only (A) is correct.**

__**Concept**__:

__
 
• Ancient modes of transportation were significantly less efficient due to reliance on animal and human power.
 
• The invention of the wheel drastically improved transportation by enabling the creation of vehicles that could carry heavier loads and travel longer distances more efficiently.

**Explanation__:**

**Efficiency of Ancient vs. Modern Transportation and Impact of the Wheel:**

__
 
• **Ancient transportation methods:** were generally slower, required significant physical labor, and had limitations on distance and load capacity.
 
• **Impact of the Wheel:** markedly transformed transportation by enabling new forms of transport that significantly improved efficiency over what was previously possible.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Transportation Efficiency:** Modern transportation benefits from advanced technologies that vastly exceed the capabilities of ancient methods.
 
• **Significant impact of the wheel:** Introduced new possibilities in transport, enabling advancements that were critical for further developments in human civilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Revolutionary Impact:** The invention of the wheel was not just a minor improvement; it was a transformative development that fundamentally changed how goods and people moved across distances.

**Comparison of Ancient and Modern Methods:** Modern methods are the result of cumulative technological advancements, making them far superior in efficiency and capability compared to ancient methods.

questions.solution:
The corect answer is __**the ability to view objects in three dimensions**__.

__
 
• Having **two eyes allows humans** to perceive **depth and distance **accurately.

questions.question: The term '*PET46'* is talked about in the context of

options.text: Genes introduced in genetically modified plants
A tiny asteroid located in the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Phys.org: **Newly discovered deep-sea enzyme breaks down PET plastic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__****PET46:**

__
 
• As part of the **PLASTISEA project** scientists at **Kiel University** have shown for the first time, using **microorganisms from the deep sea**, that polymers such as PET are continuously degraded by an enzyme.
 
• Using a metagenomic approach, the research team has identified and biochemically described the **PET-degrading enzyme PET46. *Hence option 4 is correct.***
 
• PET46 has many unusual properties and adds to the scaffold diversity of **PET-active enzymes.**
 
• Compared to the best-characterized PET-degrading enzymes from **bacteria and composting plants**, PET46 is more efficient at **70° Celsius **than these reference enzymes at their respective optimum temperatures.
 
• **Structurally, the enzyme differs significantly from those previously discovered**.
 
 
• For example, it has the ability to degrade both very long-chain PET molecules, known as polymers, and short-chain PET molecules, known as oligomers, which means that degradation can be continuous.
 
 
 
• At the molecular level, PET46 is very similar to another enzyme, ferulic acid esterase. This degrades the natural** polymer lignin in plant cell walls** by breaking down lignin polymers to release sugars from woody plant parts.
 
• Lignin and PET have many structural similarities, so the PET-degrading enzymes found in nature may be important for composting wood in forest soils, for example.
 
• The biochemical properties of PET46 therefore make it a very interesting enzyme both for** marine and terrestrial plastics** and for biotechnology.

questions.question: A gas can be converted into a liquid by -
questions.solution:
The answer is By Both.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** **Liquefaction of gases:**

__
 
• Liquefaction of gases is the process in which a gas is liquified to change its state from gas to liquid.
 
• A gases can be liquified by increasing pressure and reducing the temperature.

 
• **Effect of pressure**: When we increase the pressure, the gaseous molecule come close together.
 
• **Effect of Temperature**: When we decrease the temperature, the kinetic energy of gaseous particles decreases and they become slower.

The pressure that has to be applied as well as the temperature depends on the molecular forces of the gas molecules. Hence, a gas can be liquified by cooling or by application of pressure, or by the combining effect of both.

**Explanation:-__**

Both increasing the pressure and decreasing the temperature can convert a gas into a liquid, a process known as condensation. This is explained by the principles of the kinetic-molecular theory and phase transitions:

__
 
• By** increasing the pressure, you effectively force the gas particles closer together.**
 
• When they are** close enough to establish attractive intermolecular forces, t**he gas condenses into a liquid. An everyday example of this principle are pressure cookers, which use high pressure to cook food quicker.
 
• By** decreasing the temperature, you reduce the kinetic energy of the gas particles**, which means they move around less vigorously.
 
• When their **kinetic energy drops sufficiently, the forces of attraction between the particles overcome their kinetic energy, **and they get closer together to form a liquid.
 
• Cooling steam is an example of this process.

So, it's accurate to say that you can convert a gas into a liquid by both increasing the pressure and decreasing the temperature. However, the specifics can depend on the particular substance under consideration and the conditions it's in.

**Conclusion:-__**

So, A gas can be converted into a liquid **by both, increasing the pressure and decreasing the temperature **

When Four resistors of R Ω are connected in parallel.

questions.question: What are some ways to foster creativity in science education?
questions.solution:
Fostering creativity in science education is essential to encourage learners to think critically, explore science concepts, and approach problems in innovative ways.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Encouraging exploration and experimentation can be done by** providing learners with hands-on activities that allow them to explore science concepts in a safe and supportive environment**.
 
• This approach helps to develop curiosity and creativity, as learners are free to explore and experiment with different materials and ideas.
 
• P**romoting divergent thinking** encourages learners to **explore multiple solutions and approaches to a problem, rather than relying on a single, predetermined answer.**
 
• This helps to develop creativity and innovation, as learners are encouraged to think beyond what is presented and to explore different perspectives and possibilities.
 
• **Providing opportunities for open-ended problem-solving involves presenting learners with complex and challenging problems that require them to use critical thinking and creativity to find a solution.**
 
• This approach helps to develop problem-solving skills, as learners are required to approach problems in new and innovative ways.

**Hence, it can be concluded that all of the above options are correct.**

questions.question:
Read the following text :

When a negatively charged rod is brought near an uncharged electroscope,

(a) the electroscope leaves move further apart

(b) both the electroscope leaves acquire similar charge

(c) the negative charges pass on to the electroscope causing its leaves to move further apart

Of the above three statements:

options.text: (a) is an observation while (b) and (c) are inferences
(a) and (b) are observations and (c) is an inference

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(a) is an observation while (b) and (c) are inferences.**__

__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **(a) "the electroscope leaves move further apart" - **

 
 
• This is an **observation **that can be directly made when a negatively charged rod is brought near an uncharged electroscope.
 
• The leaves of the electroscope, being initially uncharged, repel each other when they acquire the same charge due to the presence of the negatively charged rod.
 
 
 
• **(b) "both the electroscope leaves acquire similar charge" -**
 
 
• This statement is an **inference **drawn from the observation.
 
• While it is** true that the leaves of the electroscope move further apart, indicating that they acquire the same charge (negative)**, it's an inference based on the observed behavior.
 
 
 
• **(c) "the negative charges pass on to the electroscope causing its leaves to move further apart"** -
 
 
• Similarly, this statement is an **inference **based on the observed behavior.
 
• It explains why the leaves move further apart but isn't directly observable.
 
 

Thus, **Statement (a) describes the observation, while statements (b) and (c) are inferences drawn from the observed behavior.**__

questions.question: Which among the following waves is not an electromagnetic wave?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cathode Rays.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Cathode Rays:-**

 
 
• **Cathode rays are streams of electrons emitted from the cathode (negatively charged electrode) of a vacuum tube. **
 
• They are produced when a high voltage is applied between the cathode and another electrode, called the anode (positively charged electrode).
 
• The electrons are accelerated by the electric field and travel through the vacuum tube at high speeds.
 
• **It is not an Electronic Magnetic Wave.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ultraviolet (UV) rays:-**

 
 
• **These are a type of electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths shorter than visible light and longer than X-rays. **
 
• UV rays are not visible to the human eye, but they can have a significant impact on our health and the environment.
 
• UV rays are produced by the sun, but they can also be produced by artificial sources, such as tanning beds and germicidal lamps.
 
 
 
• **Infrared (IR) rays:-**
 
 
• **These are a type of electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths longer than visible light and shorter than microwaves. **
 
• IR rays are not visible to the human eye, but we can feel them as heat.
 
• IR rays are produced by all objects with a temperature above absolute zero. The hotter the object, the more IR rays it produces.
 
 
 
• **Gamma rays:**
 
 
• **These are the most energetic type of electromagnetic radiation. **
 
• They have shorter wavelengths and higher energies than X-rays.
 
• Gamma rays are produced by radioactive decay, nuclear reactions, and certain astronomical events.
 
• Gamma rays are highly penetrating and can damage living cells. They are used in a variety of applications, such as cancer treatment, medical imaging, and materials science.

questions.question: A protein hormone is -
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**TSH.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Hormones in the human body can be broadly classified as either **steroid or protein hormones based on their chemical structure.**
 
• **Protein hormones are made up of chains of amino acids and include hormones such as insulin, growth hormone, and follicle-stimulating hormone.**
 
• **Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH), which is a protein hormone, fits into this category. **
 
• TSH is **produced and released into the bloodstream by the pituitary gland.**
 
• The primary function of **TSH is to stimulate the thyroid gland to produce thyroid hormones thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3),** which, in turn, **regulate the body's metabolism, energy production, and developmental growth.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Epinephrine (also known as adrenaline)** is a hormone and neurotransmitter. It's responsible for the fight or flight response in the body but it's not a protein hormone.
 
• **Androgens** such as testosterone, are a class of hormones that play a role in male traits and reproductive activity. They are steroid hormones produced mainly in the testes.
 
• **Progesterone** is a steroid hormone involved in the female menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryogenesis of humans and other species. It's not a protein hormone.

questions.question: Change of solid state directly to gaseous state without going through liquid state is called-
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Sublimation__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sublimation is the transition of a substance directly from the solid to the gas phase without passing through the intermediate liquid phase.

 
 
• It is an endothermic phase transition process.
 
• For example Dry ice, Naphthalene balls, etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Evaporation is a type of vaporization that occurs at the surface of a liquid as it turns into a gas phase.

 
 
• The surrounding gas should not be saturated with the evaporating substance.
 
 
 
• Condensation is the change of state of matter from the gas phase to the liquid phase, and is the opposite of evaporation.
 
• Melting point, change of solid into liquid on application of heat.
 
 
• In a pure crystalline solid, this process occurs at a certain temperature called the melting point;
 
• An impure solid typically melts at a temperature below the melting point of the main component.

questions.question: The curvature of the eye lens can be changed by
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ciliary muscles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The ability to alter the curvature of the eye's lens, a feature known as accommodation, is controlled by the ciliary muscles that are part of the eye's structure.**
 
• Ciliary muscles in the eye help change the shape of the eye's lens to allow our vision to focus on objects at various distances. 
 
• **When** **the muscles are relaxed, the curvature decreases making the lens thin and the focal length increases.**
 
• **Similarly when the ciliary muscles contract the curvature of the eye lens increases making them thicker, this decreases the focal length of the eye**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The retina, pupil, and iris are critical parts of the eye, each featuring unique functions, but they do not influence the curvature of the lens.
 
• **The retina is a layer at the back of the eyeball that contains cells sensitive to light. These cells trigger nerve impulses that pass via the optic nerve to the brain, where a visual image is formed.**
 
• The pupil is the opening in the iris that allows light to enter the retina. It changes size according to light conditions, but it doesn't affect the curvature of the lens.
 
• The iris is the colored portion of the eye that controls the amount of light that reaches the retina through the pupil. It doesn't change the lens's curvature.
